campaign: BOUNDARY/SEAL candidate freeze and safety-inventory refresh

rebinding.purpose: re-bind the OpenSSH consumer-closure evidence to the committed candidate 9046f86be and to a census regenerated at that commit
rebinding.not_an_adjudication: no obligation is discharged, reclassified or adjudicated by this document or by the closure runs it binds

binary.match_basis: the install was rebuilt at this candidate and committed with it; the on-disk bytes equal the committed bytes.

build_metadata.rebuild_recipe: bash forensics/tools/build_phase2.sh in the court container
build_metadata.rebuild_scope: cargo release build -> implemented surface -> shell -> DSOs, archives, provider module, CLI, install layout -> Phase-2 ABI courts
build_metadata.source_delta_from_previous_candidate: real code: legacy digest ctrl repairs (md_data size refusal and the legacy digest context precondition), the SSL_CONF overlapping-dispatch refusals on SslConfCtx and the prerequisite tranche
build_metadata.why: this candidate changes production code, so different artefact bytes are expected; two rebuilds at this commit produced identical bytes

checkout.kind: clean tracked tree at the candidate commit

identity.source_tree_digest_rule: sha256 over canonical JSON of sorted [relpath,size,sha256] for src/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, build.rs (forensics/tools/phase7_courts.py::_source_tree_digest)

analysis_identity.basis: sha256 over, in module-name order, each module name and a canonical JSON input record: every allocated (SHF_ALLOC) section's (name, ELF type, virtual address, size, sha256 of its bytes), the sorted relocation table (section, section-relative offset, type, canonical symbol, addend), the sorted [name, addr, size, kind] defined-symbol rows, the sorted dynamic-symbol rows, and the loader entries (SONAME/NEEDED/RUNPATH/RPATH). ``.llvm.<hash>`` and ``@@VERSION`` suffixes are canonicalised as in the symbol table; the DSO file digest is recorded as a non-identity.
analysis_identity.note: forensics/tools/consumer_closure.py at identity.tool_sha256; unchanged from v1u

reproducibility.consumer_delta: both consumers relinked against the v1w install

method.primary: compiler JSON diagnostics: `unsafe_code` lint enabled for both the lib and test targets, deduplicated by (file,line,column,kind)
method.secondary: syntax-level walk (`unsafe_census.py`, comment/literal-stripped source) for unsafe blocks, unsafe fn definitions, unsafe impls, unsafe traits and unsafe extern blocks, with production/test/seam partitioning

blind_spots: code behind an inactive cfg (target_os, feature, cfg(loom)) is not compiled and is invisible to the compiler census; the lexical walk sees it

macro_rules! bodies are counted once at the definition by the lexical walk, while the compiler lints each expansion and attributes the span to the macro; deduplication can collapse many expansions to one site
the compiler census covers src/ only because lib/tests targets are built; files unreachable from the module tree are invisible
a source-level #[allow(unsafe_code)] or a clippy allow suppresses the lint; five test modules carry such an allow and are checked lexically
unsafe_code also fires on #[no_mangle]/#[export_name]; those are compiler warnings but not census operations and are excluded here
clippy misses a SAFETY comment above a macro argument (8 observed); they are re-checked lexically and recorded as lint false positives, but they still fail the configured -D warnings gate
one lexical-only block file (src/runtime/miri_tcb.rs) is cfg-gated and invisible to the compiler at this configuration
neither mechanism proves a contract suffices; this is inventory, not discharge

definitions.BOUNDARY_COVERED: at least one production operation and every production operation matches a registered boundary predicate
definitions.PARTIAL: at least one production operation has no registered boundary
definitions.precedence: ZERO_UNSAFE is evaluated first, exactly as attribution.json does; the TEST_ONLY annotation is reported alongside, not instead

recorded.normalization_note: the recorded 6 TEST_ONLY files have zero production operations, so the zero-first rule used for the recompute counts them as ZERO_UNSAFE; this is a label difference, not a source change

contracts.scope: every file with at least one unsafe construct

method.unsafe_blocks: clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks (AST) plus structural comment attachment (contiguous comment prelude, a comment inside the same block, or a delimiter-bounded comment above a macro/call argument; a neighbouring item's SAFETY does not transfer); files containing a clippy allow are checked lexically for every block
method.unsafe_fn: structural comment attachment: SAFETY: or # Safety in the fn's contiguous leading doc/attribute prelude, or inherited from an unsafe impl/trait contract; a comment in a sibling item's body is never attached, and an attachment that cannot be decided is UNCONTRACTED (never silently contracted)
method.unsafe_impl_trait_extern: structural contiguous comment/attribute prelude must state SAFETY: or # Safety
method.attachment_rule: brace-aware: the leading region is bounded by the previous real code token and skips balanced attribute spans; every SAFETY token must not lie inside a different item's body
method.scope: every src/**/*.rs operation, production and test-only
